publications.title: The Complexity of Scheduling Pickup and Delivery Jobs
publications.abstract: Scheduling pickup and delivery jobs stands as a critical and challenging problem commonly encountered in time-sensitive logistics and transportation. Often, a large number of requests involving shipments from the same location are aggregated into either a fixed number of job queues, referred to as the queueing mode, or into a fixed number of sets, referred to as the pooling mode. Due to the time-sensitive nature, the objective of scheduling jobs by location and routing drivers is to minimize customers’ waiting times. While request aggregation is widely observed in platform economies and related research, the computational complexity of scheduling pickup and delivery jobs has not been studied. This paper presents a comprehensive complexity analysis of this problem. We prove that the problem is strongly NP-hard in the queueing mode, but is polynomially solvable in the pooling mode. Furthermore, we prove that both modes become polynomially solvable when minimizing total distance, as does the queueing mode with fixed number of drivers or scaled-length edges. Finally, we provide approximation guarantees and extend the analysis to bipartite graphs, identifying solvable variants with relaxed map-size constraints to enhance the applicability.

publications.title: Rethinking Distribution Shifts: Empirical Analysis and Modeling for Tabular Data
publications.abstract: Different distribution shifts require different interventions, and algorithms must be grounded in the specific shifts they address. However, methodological development for robust algorithms typically relies on structural assumptions that lack empirical validation. Advocating for an empirically grounded data-driven approach to algorithm development, we build an empirical testbed comprising natural shifts across 8 tabular data sets, 172 distribution pairs over 45 methods, and 90,000 method configurations encompassing empirical risk minimization and distributionally robust optimization (DRO) methods. We find that Y|X-shifts are most prevalent in our testbed, in stark contrast to the heavy focus on X (covariate)-shifts in the machine learning literature, and that the performance of robust algorithms is no better than that of vanilla methods. To understand why, we conduct an in-depth empirical analysis of DRO methods and find that underlooked implementation details—such as the choice of underlying model class (e.g., LightGBM) and hyperparameter selection—have a bigger impact on performance than the ambiguity set or its radius. We illustrate via case studies how a data-driven understanding of distribution shifts can provide a new approach to algorithm development. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08298 .

publications.title: International Journal on Cloud Computing: Services and Architecture
publications.abstract: Cloud computing helps enterprises transform business and technology. Companies have begun to look for solutions that would help reduce their infrastructures costs and improve profitability. Cloud computing is becoming a foundation for benefits well beyond IT cost savings. Yet, many business leaders are concerned about cloud security, privacy, availability, and data protection. To discuss and address these issues, we invite researches who focus on cloud computing to shed more light on this emerging field. This peer-reviewed open access Journal aims to bring together researchers and practitioners in all security aspects of cloud-centric and outsourced computing.
publications.source_detail: International Journal on Cloud Computing Services and Architecture

publications.title: İNEKLERDE SUNİ TOHUMLAMA (ST) BAŞARISINI ETKİLEYEN NEDENLER
publications.abstract: Suni Tohumlama teknolojisi, hayvancılık alanında geliştirilen en büyük biyoteknolojik yöntemlerden biri olup, sıg’ırların çiftleşmesiyle ilgili birçok problemi çözmektedir. Suni Tohumlama, ineg’in çiftleşme olmaksızın gebe bırakılması teknig’idir. Yüksek verim özelliklerine sahip bog’anın spermasının dog’rudan ineg’in uterusuna enjekte edilmesiyle gerçekleştirilir. Bu teknik, yalnızca cinsel yolla bulaşan hastalıkları önlemekle kalmaz, aynı zamanda üstün yavrular elde edilerek ıslah yapılmasını sag’lar. Ülkemizde birçok sebeplerle suni tohumlama bir türlü istenilen düzeyde yapılamamakta ayrıca kalifiye personel eksiklig’i ve yanlış uygulama nedeniyle başarı oranı da düşüktür. Bu nedenle, bu makalede, yüksek başarı elde etmek amacıyla Suni Tohumlama öncesinde, sırasında ve sonrasında yapılan (yapılması muhtemel) hatalar hakkında bilgi verilecektir.

publications.title: गोपनीयता — Bhoja's Secrecy Clause: Why the Texts Withhold Construction
publications.abstract: In the middle of chapter 31 of the Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra, after his long list of the wonders machines can perform, Bhoja stops to make a declaration: "The construction of machines has not been stated, for the sake of secrecy, not out of ignorance" (31.79cd). He gives his reasons (31.80–81): machines once exposed bring no profit and cause no wonder; what has been told are the seeds, and that, in truth, is everything. He adds that the machines he has described are to be learnt by personal instruction (31.82–83), and he names the qualifications of one who can build them: lineage, skill with instruction, study of the treatises, practice in building, effort and intelligence (31.87). This article presents these verses and reads them in three contexts: the logic of a performing machine, whose effect depends on concealment; the transmission of craft knowledge in India by lineage and guild; and the long history of the tension between secrecy and disclosure in engineering, from Hero of Alexandria and al-Jazarī, who published constructions, to the patent system, which trades disclosure for protection. The secrecy clause explains why the chapter reads as a theory and a specification rather than a manual, and it sets the terms for any modern reconstruction. Article 13 of the series Yantravidhāna Studies (SSD-31), on chapter 31 of Bhoja's Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra. Verses discussed: 31.79–88. Web version: sanskritmanthan.in/a/ssd-31-13-gopaniyata

publications.title: On the Reuse Practices in GitHub Actions Workflows
publications.abstract: Automation is fundamental to modern software engineering, with platforms such as GitHub providing built-in systems like GitHub Actions to streamline tasks across the software development lifecycle. Similar to traditional open-source software reuse, automated workflows rely heavily on reusable components such as Actions and reusable workflows. While this reliance offers significant productivity benefits, it also introduces critical dependency-related risks within the software supply chain, particularly regarding security vulnerabilities and maintainability. To address these overlooked challenges, this PhD dissertation presents a comprehensive empirical investigation into automation and reuse practices within the GitHub Actions ecosystem. Employing a mixed-methods approach, it combines qualitative survey findings from workflow practitioners with large-scale software repository mining. Through this empirical lens, the research evaluates workflow reuse behaviours, quantifies component outdatedness, maps complex dependency networks, and assesses ecosystem-wide security dimensions. The findings reveal key motivations and selection criteria behind workflow reuse while uncovering widespread vulnerability exposure and maintenance challenges. Ultimately, this work provides actionable guidance and insights for practitioners, tool developers, and researchers to foster a more secure, reliable, and maintainable workflow automation ecosystem.

publications.title: A Lightweight Selective Classification Framework for Music-Centric YouTube Videos Using Audio Repetition and Metadata
publications.abstract: Music-centric video selection for karaoke differs from detecting the presence of music: films, trailers, cookingvideos, and travel montages can contain highly repetitive soundtracks while serving a non-musical purpose.This exploratory study documents a lightweight pipeline combining traditional chroma-based repetitioncoverage, short-lag periodicity, YouTube category exclusions, and a reject option for human review. Noneural network, large language model, or pretrained audio classifier is used for prediction. Audio indicatorsare normalized using selection-set percentiles, combined with fixed candidate weights, and evaluated withselection-calibrated dual thresholds. The research progressed from a 50-item pilot experiment to threeexploratory batches totaling 323 videos, with a 273-item speech-reduced replay and a 229-item historicalholdout. On that repeatedly inspected holdout, the pure-coverage configuration with category filtering andselective Entertainment review automatically classified 190 videos, rejected 39, and made 11 automatic errors:coverage 82.97% and selective risk 5.79%. Entertainment protection intercepted eight music-backed falsepositives while additionally rejecting one correctly classified song. These results do not meet the strict risktarget below 5%. Repeated reuse of historical data, provisional labels, unresolved recording-independenceevidence, and convenience sampling prevent independent validation claims. The contribution is an auditableengineering combination and empirical diagnosis, not a new theory of chroma, repetition, or selectiveclassification.

publications.title: Embedding Gender Perspectives in LIS Programmes: Recommendations Report — WP3
publications.abstract: This report presents 15 actionable recommendations for embedding gender perspectives in Library and Information Science (LIS) programmes. It is an output of the Erasmus+ project GEDIS (Gender Diversity in Information Science: Challenges in Higher Education). The recommendations are based on the project’s findings at seven European partner institutions in Spain, Germany, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Austria and Czechia. These findings include 28 focus groups, partner context reports, documented good practices, identified barriers and criteria for good practice. The recommendations are addressed to programme coordinators, teachers and institutions at three levels: Curricula: map where gender appears; anchor it in core LIS topics such as users, knowledge organisation, collections, ethics and AI; include technical courses; write it into learning outcomes; and set guidance for reading lists and citation. Teaching strategies: use active and reflective methods; review examples and materials for stereotypes; plan participation; agree communication rules; and make assessment expectations explicit. Institutional policies: offer short, discipline-specific training; provide practical resources and language guidance; set clear procedures for students’ names and gender identity; recognise committed teachers; and monitor progress. Each recommendation builds on practices already used by at least one partner and is linked to the barriers and criteria it addresses. The report also sets priorities for different contexts: foundational awareness where the environment is conservative; programme-level embedding where equality plans exist but do not reach teaching; integration into course content where awareness is already high

publications.title: MRIReco.jl test and documentation data
publications.abstract: Data used by the tests and the documentation of MRIReco.jl. Each tarball is a lazy Julia artifact: MRIRecoTestData.tar.gz for the tests of MRIFiles, MRIRecoDocsData.tar.gz for the tutorials and examples of the documentation. The files come from different sources and keep the licence of their source. README.md lists provenance and licence of every file. In short: CC BY 4.0 for own data and the kidney and mouse slices (doi:10.5281/zenodo.4762380, doi:10.5281/zenodo.10610639); CC BY-NC 4.0 for the knee slice from mridata.org; ISMRMRD Software License for the ISMRMRD example files.

publications.title: Pendataan Berbasis Aplikasi Digital dan Pemetaan Geospasial Masjid di Kecamatan Tangerang dan Karawaci
publications.abstract: This article evaluates the digital field inventory and geospatial location auditing of mosques conducted by Student Community Service (KKM) Group 2 of STISNU Nusantara Tangerang in collaboration with LP2KU MUI and BAZNAS Tangerang City across Tangerang and Karawaci Districts. Based on a participatory census approach updated as of 28 September 2026, the inventory documented 105 mosques and musallas (56 in Tangerang District and 49 in Karawaci District) out of 149 benchmark targets from the Tangerang City One Data Web 2025, achieving an overall coverage rate of 70.5% (75.7% in Tangerang and 65.3% in Karawaci) across 24 urban villages, with 6 villages achieving 100% recording completion. Land utilization analysis indicates that 76 mosques (72.4%) operate on Waqf land, 27 mosques (25.7%) stand on public amenities land (Fasos/Fasum), 1 mosque (0.95%) occupies government-permitted land, and 1 mosque (0.95%) holds a Sale and Purchase Deed (AJB). Geospatial verification confirmed that 100% of entries possess valid Latitude-Longitude coordinates passing format and location completeness checks without exact coordinate duplications. These findings recommend leveraging the BAZNAS Menara Masjid platform for geospatial data integration and structured land certification support in coordination with local government agencies.
